q: 1. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in
explain: Thin walls (thickness < 10cm or half-brick) and decorative honey-comb brickwork are measured by superficial area (m²) rather than volume.

q: 2. In the center line method of working out volumes, for cross walls, what deductions must be made from the center line length at each junction?
explain: At each 'T' junction, a length equal to half the breadth of the wall is deducted from the total center line length to avoid double counting the corners.

q: 3. In long and short wall method of estimation, the length of long wall is the center to center distance between the walls and
options: half breadth of wall on each side
one fourth breadth of wall on each side
explain: Length of long wall = (c/c distance) + (2 * half breadth) = c/c distance + full breadth of wall.

q: 4. The unit of payment for excavation in trenches for pipes, cables etc, upto 1.5m depth in ordinary rock/hard rock is in
explain: As noted previously for utility trenching, the standard unit of payment is often the linear meter for specific depth ranges.

q: 5. The unit of measurement of masonry work (ashlar and rubble) is
explain: Stone masonry, whether ashlar (dressed) or rubble (undressed), is a volumetric item measured in cubic meters (m³).

q: 6. A fixed stated sum of penalty to help by contractor having definite relationship with real damage is
explain: Liquidated damages are a pre-estimated sum agreed upon in the contract to be paid if the contractor fails to complete the work on time.

q: 7. The item of steel work which is measured in sq. m is
explain: Items like rolling shutters and steel doors are typically measured by their clear area in square meters (m²).

q: 8. Pick up the correct statement from the following
options: pointing is measures in sq. m
plastering is measures in sq. m
striking is measures in sq. m
explain: All surface-finishing works like pointing, plastering, and formwork striking are measured by area (m²).

q: 9. The unit of measurement for earth work in excavation in ordinary soils, earth work in mixed soil with kankar, bajri etc. when depth of excavation does not exceed 30 cm is
explain: Surface excavation or 'surface dressing' not exceeding 30 cm in depth is measured in square meters (m²).

q: 10. One hectare-meter represent a volume of
explain: 1 Hectare = 10,000 m². Therefore, 1 Hectare-meter = 10,000 m² * 1 m = 10,000 m³.

q: 11. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate, is
options: Location of site and local labour charges
explain: A detailed estimate must account for physical quantities as well as logistical factors like material transport and regional labor rates.

q: 12. How many kilo-liters are there in one cubic meter?
explain: 1 m³ = 1000 liters. Since 1000 liters = 1 kilo-liter (kL), then 1 m³ = 1 kL.

q: 13. The number of corrugations in a galvanized corrugated sheet usually
explain: The most common configuration for standard commercial GI roofing sheets is 10 corrugations per sheet width.

q: 14. The plinth area method is also known as
explain: The plinth area estimate is calculated by multiplying the area (in sq. ft or sq. m) by a rate, hence 'square rate method'.

q: 15. Carpet area does not include the area of
options: the walls along with doors and other openings
explain: Carpet area is the net usable floor area excluding walls, circulation areas (corridors), and sanitary blocks.

q: 16. In standard notation which of the following is prismoidal formula for earthwork calculations
explain: The prismoidal formula (Simpson's Rule) for volume between two sections with a mid-section area $A_m$ is $V =  rac{L}{6}(A_1 + 4A_m + A_2)$.

q: 17. An area of one hectare is equal to
explain: By definition, 1 Hectare is the area of a square with 100m sides: $100 	imes 100 = 10,000 	ext{ m}^2$.

q: 18. The correct prismoidal formula for volume is
options: D/3 [first area + last area + Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 4Σ even area + 2Σ odd areas]
D/3 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
D/6 [first area + last area + 2Σ even area + 4Σ odd areas]
explain: The prismoidal formula (also known as Simpson's rule for volume) uses the coefficients 1, 4, 2, 4... 1. It is expressed as $V = \frac{D}{3} [A_1 + A_n + 4(\text{even areas}) + 2(\text{remaining odd areas})]$.

q: 19. In what units are the quantities for the frames of doors and windows computed
explain: Door and window frames (Chaukhats) are made of timber and are measured by their total volume in cubic meters (m³).

q: 20. The correct relationship between rise, R and tread, T is
explain: A standard rule of thumb for comfortable stair design is that twice the rise plus the tread (in mm) should equal approximately 600 mm (2R + T = 600).

q: 21. No deductions is made in the masonry for the opening in the area of the opening does not exceed
explain: According to IS 1200, small openings like holes for pipes or vents up to 0.1 m² (1000 sq. cm) are not deducted from the total masonry volume.

q: 22. While estimating for plastering usually no deduction is made for
explain: Small surface interruptions like beam ends, rafter ends, or tiny openings are not deducted because the labor saved is offset by the labor required to finish the edges.

q: 23. The main factor to be considered while preparing a detailed estimate is
explain: A detailed estimate must account for the volume of material, its market availability, and the cost to transport it to the site (lead charges).

q: 24. The size of the standard modular brick is
explain: The actual size of a modular brick is 19 x 9 x 9 cm. When mortar joints (1 cm) are added, the nominal size becomes 20 x 10 x 10 cm.

q: 25. The unit of measurement of roofing (each and every detail specified) is
explain: Roofing work (sheets, tiles, or slabs) is measured by the net planar area covered, expressed in square meters (m²).

q: 26. Whenever the whitewashing or distempering is done on corrugated iron sheets, in the estimation the plan area the sheets is increased by
explain: Because of the 'waves' in corrugated sheets, the actual surface area is greater than the plan area. For standard GI sheets, a 14% increase is applied.

q: 27. In case of grills, for the estimation of painted area, the flat area is multiplied by
explain: To account for both sides and the intricate edges of a steel grill, the front area is doubled (multiplied by 2) to find the total painting area.

q: 28. In case of steel rolling shutters, for the estimation of painted area, the plain area is multiplied by
explain: Rolling shutters have a corrugated profile. To estimate the painting area for one side, the flat area is multiplied by 1.1 or 1.25 (1 1/4) depending on the corrugation depth.

q: 29. For 100 square metres of plastered surface, the quantity of lime required for one coat of white washing will be ............
explain: Standard estimating norms for civil works specify that approximately 115 m2 of lime (as a unit of measurement for material consumption in specific regions) is required for 100 m2 of plastering to account for surface absorption and texture.

q: 30. The unit of measurement of railing is ............
explain: Railings for stairs, balconies, or corridors are typically measured in running meters (per m) as the height is usually standard, making the length the primary variable.

q: 31. The supply of paint, varnish and enamel is measured in ............
explain: Liquid finishing materials like paints, varnishes, and enamels are commercially supplied and estimated in liters (ltr).

q: 32. The unit of measurement of aluminium partition is ............
explain: Aluminum partitions are measured by the area they cover, which is calculated in square meters (m2).

q: 33. The quantity of cement concrete damp-proofing course is measured in terms of ............
explain: Damp-proofing course (DPC) has a specified thickness; therefore, it is measured by area in square meters (m2).

q: 34. The unit of measurement of turfing in embankment is called ............
explain: Turfing (planting grass) involves covering the surface area of the embankment slopes, hence it is measured in square meters (m2).

q: 35. The unit of measurement of site clearance in irrigation canal is ............
explain: Large scale site clearance involving earthwork volumes in canal construction is often measured in cubic meters (m3), though surface clearance is sometimes m2.

q: 36. The areas of a sloping surface of a protective embankment of mean height d, side slopes S : 1 and length L is ............
explain: Using Pythagoras theorem for the slope length (sqrt(d^2 + (sd)^2)) and multiplying by the length (L), the formula simplifies to L * d * sqrt(1 + s^2).

q: 37. The essential requirements to prepare a good estimate are ............
options: a full dimensioned drawing to scale
explain: A comprehensive estimate requires geometric data (drawings), quality standards (specifications), and unit costs (schedule of rates).

q: 38. The quantity of wood for the shutters of doors and windows is calculated in ............
explain: While the frame (chowkhat) is measured in m3, the shutters are measured by the area they cover in square meters (m2).

q: 39. The quantity of partition walls and honey-comb walls are worked out in ............
explain: Thin walls, such as half-brick partitions or honey-comb brickwork, are typically estimated by their surface area in m2 rather than volume.

q: 40. The quantity for expansion joint in building is worked out in ............
explain: Expansion joints are typically measured by their length in running meters (m).

q: 41. The unit of measurement of earth in filling ............
explain: Earthwork, whether for excavation or filling, is a volumetric task and is measured in cubic meters (m3).

q: 42. The unit of measurement of 75 mm thick P.C.C. is ............
explain: Concrete work with a specified thickness (usually 100mm or less) is measured by area in m2.

q: 43. The unit measurement of R.C.C. works in shelves of jail (thickness and type specified) is .........
explain: Thin R.C.C. members like shelves or fins with a specified thickness are measured in m2.

q: 44. The R.C.C. work in beam, slab and lintel is measured in ............
explain: Standard structural R.C.C. components like beams and slabs are calculated by their total volume in cubic meters (m3).

q: 45. The unit of measurement of welding and soldering of plates is ............
explain: Welding and soldering are measured by the linear length of the joint, which is per meter (per m).but as per key quintal

q: 46. If the bearing is not specified for the lintel, in the estimation it is usually taken as ............
options: thickness of lintel subjected to minimum value of 12 cm
3/4 of lintel thickness or 12 cm whichever is large
explain: If not specified, the end bearing of a lintel should be equal to the thickness of the lintel or 12cm, whichever is greater (common convention is often cited as 3/4 to full thickness).

q: 47. In the estimation of plastering surface the deductions are not made for ............
explain: According to IS 1200, no deductions are made for ends of beams, rafters, or small openings less than 0.5 m2 when calculating plastering area.

q: 48. The unit of measurement of holdfast is ............
explain: Holdfasts are iron fixtures, and like most structural steel or iron items, they are measured by weight in kilograms (kg) or quintals.

q: 49. The unit of measurement of rainwater pipe heads fixed on position is ............
explain: Standard fittings or fixtures like pipe heads are counted numerically ('each').

q: 50. The document unit of measurement of binding wire in R.C.C. work is measured in ............
explain: Binding wire is typically calculated as a percentage of steel weight or measured in weight units like quintals (100 kg).
